prompt: How many solutions does the system $2x + 3y = 12$ and $4x + 6y = 24$ have?
hint: Compare the two equations. Is one a multiple of the other?

hints.text: Compare the two equations. Is one a multiple of the other?
Multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives exactly the second.
They are the same line, so every point on it is a solution: infinitely many.

learningObjective: Recognize a dependent system from proportional coefficients.
explanation: Multiply the first equation by $2$: $4x + 6y = 24$ — identical to the second.
Two identical equations describe the same line, so every point on that line satisfies both.
The system has infinitely many solutions.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the ratios
steps: All three ratios equal means the same line: infinitely many solutions. All three equal *except* the constant means parallel lines: no solutions.
This ratio check answers every "how many solutions" question in about ten seconds, without solving anything.
